transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Alex Romero (CTO, Scion), Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng), Tom Burke (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto generated, may be rough):
Scion describes a streaming assistant use-case with heavy concurrency and low p95 needs. They want benchmarks across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Redwood AE/SE asked about token distributions and current infra, offered tradeoffs: hosted quick-start vs dedicated for predictable latency and private for compliance. Discussed KV cache, prefix caching, batching, quantization impacts, and fallback model variants.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll run 45 minutes and save time for a recap. quick intro, i'm maya, ae on infra, and devon is our se who will dig into the throughput details.
00:18 Alex: great, thanks, i can give context. we're scion, building a streaming assistant for enterprise search — typical turn is 200 to 800 tokens but we have shorter quick queries too. our p95 target for short queries is, ah, ideally 200 to 250 ms end-to-end.
00:35 Priya: yeah and for longer flows we expect up to 4k tokens across a conversation, but the important metric is concurrent active streams — we're planning for 5k steady concurrency with bursts up to 12k during events.
00:50 Devon: ok, that's helpful. when you say 200-250ms p95, is that token emission latency or end-to-end response?
01:01 Alex: end-to-end from client send to first meaningful token surfaced. includes our frontend + network.
01:09 Maya: got it. so there are a few levers — hosted can be fast for most customers but p95 can vary with noisy multi-tenant spikes. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools which smooths p95 and predictable coldstart behavior. Private gives the tightest network control but you trade operational ownership.
01:30 Tom: couple clarifying things — we need SOC2 and KMS for keys, plus audit logs. also we have VPC peering needs for private.
01:40 Maya: yep, we have a SOC2 pack and KMS/HSM integration for Private; we'll share those docs. also audit logs are available in Redwood Console with token-level traces (note: transcription sometimes says con-soul or console).
01:55 Priya: on the performance side, do you have numbers for p95 on Hosted for short prompts?
02:05 Devon: rough numbers — depends on model size and sequence length. for a 13B-ish open model at ~256 tokens we often see p95 around 150-300ms in hosted, but it depends on region and current multi-tenant load. Dedicated can drop p95 variance and get you closer to 120-200ms with proper HW and batching config.
02:30 Alex: and stream performance? we need low-latency token streaming — can you do continuous batching without stalling first token?
02:40 Devon: yes, our runtime supports continuous batching and streaming — we prioritize first-token latency by preemptive small-batch scheduling, and then aggregate subsequent tokens into larger batches for throughput. there's tradeoffs; if you push for absolute lowest first-token p95 you'll lose some aggregate tokens/sec.
03:00 Priya: what about KV cache / prefix caching? a lot of our work is context reuse across streams, it'd help a lot.
03:10 Devon: we have automatic KV caching for repeated contexts, and prefix cache to reduce compute on repeated system prompts. with that, you can reduce per-token compute by, roughly, 10–40% depending on reuse. note: sometimes transcriptions say k-v cash or kv cache as 'k v cache' which is fine.
03:32 Tom: our main worry is burst autoscaling — if we go hosted, will p95 spike during unpredicted bursts?
03:40 Maya: there are two mechanisms — hosted is multi-tenant with elastic capacity, so bursts are handled but p95 variability can happen. Dedicated with reserved pools gives you consistent tail latency; you can also configure burst capacity in Dedicated to allow temporary overcommit to hosted pool. we also support routing policies to fallback to smaller model variants during overload.
04:05 Alex: smaller model variants = quality tradeoff, of course. how does Redwood suggest balancing quantization and p95?
04:15 Devon: quantization (int8/int4) reduces memory and can increase throughput, sometimes at minor quality loss. we recommend per-workload evals. Redwood Optimize can produce quantization recommendations; the SE can run comparative runs with your prompts to show quality delta.
04:35 Priya: can we do an A/B across hosted and dedicated with the same prompts to see real-world p95 differences?
04:43 Maya: yes, we can set up a short pilot — you'll get a Hosted baseline and we'll run a Dedicated instance with the same model and prompt set. we'll also provide tooling to replay your traffic or give a small harness.
04:58 Alex: about token/sec and sustained throughput — our peak sustained during tests is around 1.2M tokens/sec (aggregate) and we need to know what that means in terms of cluster sizing.
05:12 Devon: okay that's aggregate. so if you're doing streaming with smaller tokens per request, the important number is concurrent streams and per-stream token emission rate. for example, 5k concurrent streams at ~5 tokens/sec each is 25k tokens/sec sustained; your 1.2M sounds like event peaks, is that right?
05:30 Priya: yes, 1.2M was total across all services during a synthetic load — our real steady-state target is lower but we want headroom.
05:38 Devon: we'll run two types of microbenchmarks: token emission microbench on a Dedicated pool and a concurrency streaming run with your client to measure real-world first-token and subsequent token p95.
05:50 Tom: what about cold starts? if a Dedicated autoscaler spins new workers, does that impact p95 severely?
06:00 Devon: we expose coldstart characteristics — dedicated pools can be configured with minimum warm instances per model or utilize warm pool keeps to keep a certain number of cards ready to accept traffic. coldstarts typically cost a few 100s of ms for model load depending on quantization and model size; warm pools reduce that.
06:18 Alex: network path — we need to ensure VPC peering won't add jitter; for private we control networking end-to-end, right?
06:26 Maya: yes Private gives you customer-managed networking; hosted uses regional public endpoints, Dedicated can be VPC-integrated. we'll need to coordinate on peering topology in the follow-up with your network team.
06:40 Priya: for benchmarking, do you want sample prompts now or should we upload to the test harness?
06:46 Alex: we'll upload a 10k prompt workload that includes short queries and longer policy docs.
06:52 Maya: perfect. please include token distributions per prompt and a flag for streaming vs non-streaming. that helps SE configure batch windows and safe concurrency caps.
07:05 Priya: question on failure modes — if a model hits a token budget, do you have graceful degradation?
07:12 Devon: yes — we have fallback policies: model variant fallback, region fallback, and canary rollouts with automatic rollback on quality regressions. you can set per-route policies via the Console. sometimes the transcriber shows route as root, but it's per-route in the product.
07:32 Tom: audits & logs — we want token-level cost attribution and traceability.
07:38 Maya: Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route, plus trace hooks. For private you can ship logs to your SIEM or use our audit export.
07:50 Alex: competition wise, we've looked at Anthropic and openai. ours plans include potential building internally but the time-to-market is worrying.
07:58 Maya: yep that's common; Redwood's goal is to reduce ops for you while giving controls.
08:05 Priya: can you explain batching windows and their effect on p95 vs throughput?
08:12 Devon: batching window is how long runtime waits to aggregate requests into a batch. smaller window => lower latency but less efficient GPU utilization; larger window increases tokens/sec but increases p95. we apply adaptive batching that grows the batch when throughput increases and shrinks when latency sensitivity is detected. it's not perfect; we can tune per-route.
08:36 Alex: what metrics should we capture during your benchmark?
08:40 Devon: capture first-token p50/p95/p99, per-token emission latency, CPU/GPU utilization, batch sizes over time, KV cache hit rate, and request concurrency. also measure end-to-end client RTT so you can separate network from model time.
09:00 Priya: can you do streaming with stateful context where KV cache persists across streams?
09:07 Devon: yes, KV cache and persistent per-user contexts are supported; you'll want to size the memory footprint and we can recommend quantization and eviction policies.
09:20 Tom: any gotchas with quantized models and streaming?
09:24 Devon: sometimes int4 quant can slightly affect generation quality and may change perf characteristics for attention kernels. that's why we recommend comparative evals. plus some runtime kernels are optimized differently for int8 vs fp16.
09:38 Alex: hypothetical — if we want deterministic p95 of <250ms for 90% of time for short prompts, what's your suggested path?
09:46 Maya: start with Hosted to get baseline, run a short Dedicated pilot with a reserved pool sized for your peak concurrency. configure warm pools and small batching windows, enable prefix caching, and run traffic replay. if you need absolute determinism and network control, move to Private but that requires more ops.
10:05 Priya: what about pricing — do you charge for reserved GPUs plus usage?
10:10 Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit) plus usage for burst; Hosted is usage-based. Private is enterprise licensing plus support. we'll send a simple model for comparison.
10:20 Alex: ok, next steps: we'll upload the prompt set and the test harness config. can you run an initial Dedicated microbench?
10:26 Devon: yes, i'll kick off a token/sec microbench and a streaming concurrency run once we have prompt set. expect results in 3–5 business days.
10:35 Maya: we'll also send security docs and SOC2 artifacts.
10:40 Tom: can you include a thread about VPC peering steps?
10:44 Maya: yes, add networking checklist to next steps.
10:47 Priya: last question — how do you measure p95 during streaming? is it time to first meaningful token or some token index?
10:55 Devon: typically first-token latency is used for streaming p95. we also report per-token emission latency for tokens 2..n, and aggregate per-sequence completion times.
11:10 Alex: ok thanks, sounds good.
11:15 Maya: quick recap and owners — maya will send pricing and SOC2, devon runs the microbench, priya uploads prompts. we should meet again after devon's run.
11:28 Priya: we'll aim to have prompts up by monday.
11:32 Tom: network team will be available for a deep-dive next week.
11:35 Maya: perfect, we'll book follow-up. thanks all.

Notes / imperfections seen in transcription: speaker labels occasionally shifted, product names sometimes altered ("Redwood Console" transcribed as "con-soul"), acronyms like KV cache and p95 sometimes spaced or spelled out. filler words present.

- Benchmarks: Devon will run token/sec microbench and streaming concurrency run on Dedicated; sample harness & prompts to be uploaded by Scion.
